newsitem.title: UK: Woolwich shares could top 324p on debut.
newsitem.headline: Woolwich shares could top 324p on debut.

text.p: Shares in the Woolwich Building Society to be floated on Monday are expected to close their first day of trade between 316-324p, according to financial bookmaker IG Index.
The Woolwich is the latest building society to demutualise, following the Halifax and Alliance & Leicester flotations earlier this year.
Dealers said they expected the shares to open around 310-320p but added that they were cautious as to how the shares would perform longer-term.

"We are not sure the shares will perform in the same fashion as the Halifax and Alliance & Leicester," said one senior dealer. "The rating, at 20 times earnings, is very demanding and a lot higher than the others."

Shares in the Halifax and Alliance & Leicester both topped market expectations in initial trade to open at 774-1/2p and 542-1/2p respectively. The Halifax was currently trading at 777p whilst Alliance was quoted at 616p on Friday.
The Woolwich is expected to command a market capitalisation of over 5 billion stg, placing it firmly among Britain's top 100 companies.

The building society's likely entry into London's leading FTSE 100 share index will secure demand for the stock from index tracker funds who need to maintain weightings in all top stocks to match the performance of the index overall.
Dealers said this demand would prove supportive but they commented that the share price may drift off in the interim period before the new shares officially gain entry into the index.

"The tracker funds and institutions will probably have to get involved because Woolwich will be a FTSE stock and they will need to maintain weightings," one dealer said. "But there will be some delay before the Woolwich reaches the FTSE."
The building society said on Friday that it would sell 370 million shares, representing 23 percent of the issued share capital in four auctions arranged by broker BZW.
The Woolwich said all members who elected to sell their entitlement of free shares in the auctions would receive the same price per share based on the average sale proceeds.
